_how_to_fill: Fill each entry following references/writing-descriptions.md in the bi-joe-data-profiler skill. source: system_metadata | user_documentation | inferred | pending. When source is inferred, confidence (high|medium|low) and evidence are required. The description is plain business language: no column names, IDs or backticks, and it must say more than the name does. grain builds on it ('One row for each ...'). Suggest BEAM annotations in beam{} following references/beam-annotations-guide.md. Then run: bijoe check <dir> and bijoe render <dir>.

dataset.summary: Retail sales of footwear through a chain of company-run shops in the United States, covering the people who buy, the shoes on offer and the shops that sell them. Purchases run from January 2025 to October 2026.
evidence: `Stores.State` has 8 distinct US state codes; `Customers.State` has 11; all `Stores.StoreName` values start with 'StepUp'
`Products.Category` has 8 values including Sandals, Kids, Running, Hiking, Boots
`Sales.StoreID` is filled on every row and matches `Stores.StoreID` 100%; there is no online-channel column

Customers.description: A person who has bought from the company at least once and belongs to its loyalty programme, together with the shop they prefer and whether they agreed to receive emails.
Customers.grain: One row for each person who has signed up as a customer
evidence: `CustomerID` unique, 0% missing, 200 rows, values C00001 onward
`TotalOrders` min 1 and `LifetimeSpend` min 32.68 for all 200 rows, so every customer has bought at least once
`LoyaltyTier` always filled, 4 values: Gold (59), Platinum (49), Bronze (47), Silver (45)
`FirstName`, `LastName`, `BirthDate` (1955-05-14 to 2008-08-26), `Gender`, `Email`, `Phone` describe an individual, not a company
`PreferredStoreID` found in `Stores.StoreID` for 200 of 200 values (measured relationship)
`EmailOptIn` True (127), False (73)

Checked separately with an ad-hoc script: 9 of 200 customers have no row in `Sales`; `TotalOrders` equals the number of distinct `Sales.TransactionID` for only 7 of 191 customers that do; `LifetimeSpend` equals the sum of `Sales.TotalPrice` for 0 customers
open_questions: Which period do `TotalOrders` and `LifetimeSpend` cover, and in which currency is `LifetimeSpend`? Are they calculated from more sales than the `Sales` table holds?
Is `Gender` value Other really 63 of 200 customers, or does it mean not stated?
What does `EmailOptIn` consent to: marketing emails, receipts, or both?
Customers.ai_notes: `TotalOrders` and `LifetimeSpend` are totals stored on the customer, not derived from the `Sales` table: the sales rows of a customer never add up to `LifetimeSpend` (checked separately). `Gender` has three values, M (72), F (65) and Other (63), where Other is unusually frequent. `SignupDate` runs 2018-01-26 to 2026-09-17, and no customer has a sale before their sign-up date (checked separately). `Phone` uses the 555 exchange and `Email` uses mail.test and example.com domains, which suggests the contact data is not real.

beam.table_why: One row per `CustomerID`, no validity dates, version columns or current flag, so each customer holds a single set of current values.

CustomerID.why: The identifier that tells one customer row from another; filled on all 200 rows and unique.

FirstName.why: A person's name is needed on every customer row.

LastName.why: A person's name is needed on every customer row.

BirthDate.why: A person's date of birth should not change.

SignupDate.why: The date a person signed up happens once and should not change.

PreferredStoreID.why: Measured relationship to `Stores.StoreID`, 200 of 200 values found.

TotalOrders.why: A count that can be summed across customers. It is a stored total on the customer, not an event.

LifetimeSpend.why: A stored total of money spent, summable across customers. Currency is not stated, so no unit is given.

Products.description: A shoe the company sells, in a particular colour and material, with its brand, intended wearer, selling price, what it costs the company and the quantity in stock.
Products.grain: One row for each shoe model in a particular colour and material
evidence: `ProductID` unique, 0% missing, 60 rows; `SKU` also unique (format SKU-639131)

`ProductName` has 58 distinct values in 60 rows; 'Velora Glide Boots' appears 3 times, with different `Color`/`Material` (Grey Suede, Green Suede, Blue Leather) and different `UnitPrice` (98.99, 113.99, 139.99). Checked separately: the combination `ProductName` + `Color` + `Material` is unique across all 60 rows
`SizeRange` has 3 values (7-14: 32, 6-12: 19, 1-7: 9), so a row is not one size
`UnitCost` is below `UnitPrice` on all 60 rows (checked separately)
`Gender` values Women (19), Unisex (17), Men (15), Kids (9); `Category` Kids (9) always pairs with `Gender` Kids (checked separately)
`StockQty` 4 to 498; `IsActive` True (54), False (6)
`Sales.ProductID` matches `Products.ProductID` 100% (measured relationship)
open_questions: What does `IsActive` = False mean: discontinued, paused or hidden from sale?
As of which date is `StockQty` measured, and is it stock across all shops or a central warehouse?
In which currency are `UnitPrice` and `UnitCost` stated, and does `UnitCost` include freight and duties?
Products.ai_notes: `UnitPrice` here is the current list price; `Sales.UnitPrice` equals it on all 2,535 sales rows (checked separately), so either prices never changed or the sales rows copy the current price. `StockQty` is a single snapshot of stock on hand. `LaunchDate` runs 2020-02-23 to 2026-11-19, and no sale is dated before its product's launch (checked separately). 8 of the 60 products never appear in `Sales`, and none of the 6 inactive products was sold (checked separately).

beam.table_why: One row per `ProductID` with no validity dates, version columns or current flag, so only current values are held.

ProductID.why: The identifier that tells one product row from another; filled and unique across 60 rows.

SKU.why: A stock-keeping code like SKU-639131 that people use in the real world to identify the product; unique and always filled.

LaunchDate.why: The date a product was launched should not change.

UnitPrice.why: A unit price is never summed. The currency is not stated.

UnitCost.why: A unit cost is a per-item rate, not summable. The currency is not stated.

StockQty.why: Stock on hand is a level at one point in time, so it can be summed across products but not over time.

Stores.description: A shop where the company sells shoes to customers, with its address, manager, size, number of staff and the date it opened.
evidence: `StoreID` unique, 0% missing, 15 rows, values S001 onward
`Address`, `ZipCode`, `Phone`, `Manager` each unique across 15 rows; `OpenDate` 2010-10-14 to 2024-02-28
`StoreType` values Outlet (6), Flagship (4), Kiosk (3), Standard (2)
`Sales.StoreID` and `Customers.PreferredStoreID` each match `Stores.StoreID` 100% (measured relationships)
`StoreName` has 14 distinct values in 15 rows: 'StepUp Northpoint Houston' appears twice (types Standard and Outlet); all names begin with 'StepUp'
open_questions: Are the two shops named 'StepUp Northpoint Houston' really two locations, or is one a data-entry duplicate or a renamed shop?
Does `Employees` count all staff or only current full-time staff, and as of which date?
Stores.ai_notes: Two shops share the name 'StepUp Northpoint Houston' but differ in `StoreType` (Standard, Outlet) and in address, so the name alone does not identify a shop; `StoreID` does. `Employees` has 14 distinct values from 8 to 40 across 15 shops. No online or warehouse location appears here.

beam.table_why: One row per `StoreID` with no validity dates, version columns or current flag, so only current values are held.

StoreID.why: The identifier that tells one shop from another; filled and unique across 15 rows.

OpenDate.why: The date a shop opened should not change.

SquareFeet.why: The column name states square feet, a unit of area.

Employees.why: A head count at a point in time: can be summed across shops, not across time.

Sales.description: One product line rung up in a shop on a customer's purchase: which shoe, how many, the price, any discount and the amount charged. A purchase can have several lines.
Sales.grain: One row for each product line on a purchase
evidence: `SaleLineID` unique, 0% missing, 2,535 rows

`TransactionID` has 1,600 distinct values in 2,535 rows, at most 4 rows each; `SaleDateTime`, `StoreID` and `CustomerID` are identical within each `TransactionID` (checked separately), so `TransactionID` is the purchase and a row is a line on it
`SaleDateTime` min 2025-01-01 12:18:13, max 2026-10-31 10:34:00, one value per purchase (1,600 distinct)
`TotalPrice` = `Quantity` x `UnitPrice` - `Discount` on all 2,535 rows (checked separately), so `Discount` is an amount, not a percentage; `Discount` is 0 on 1,674 rows
`StoreID`, `ProductID` and `CustomerID` match `Stores.StoreID`, `Products.ProductID` and `Customers.CustomerID` for 100% of filled values (measured relationships)
`CustomerID` is missing on 891 of 2,535 rows (35.15%)
open_questions: Why is `CustomerID` empty on 35.15% of sale lines: customers who did not identify themselves or did not join the loyalty programme?
Is `TotalPrice` before or after tax, and in which currency are `UnitPrice`, `Discount` and `TotalPrice` stated?
How is `Discount` decided (promotion, loyalty tier, manual markdown)? No column says why.
Sales.ai_notes: `CustomerID` is empty on 35.15% of rows. `UnitPrice` equals `Products.UnitPrice` on every row (checked separately). `TotalPrice` is `Quantity` x `UnitPrice` - `Discount` with no tax column, so it is probably before tax (not confirmed). `Discount` values include whole amounts (5, 10, 15, 20) and cent-level amounts (e.g. 2.3, 3.45), up to 131.99. No sale is before the customer's sign-up date or the product's launch date, and no inactive product was sold (checked separately).

beam.table_why: Each row is a sale line that happens at one moment (`SaleDateTime`) and is finished once rung up; there are no later milestone dates.

SaleLineID.why: The identifier that tells one sale line from another; filled and unique across 2,535 rows.

TransactionID.why: A purchase number shared by up to 4 lines, with no table of its own (no measured relationship from it).

SaleDateTime.why: The moment the purchase was rung up; filled on every row.

StoreID.why: The shop where the sale happened; measured relationship to `Stores.StoreID` 100%.

CustomerID.why: The customer the purchase is linked to; measured relationship to `Customers.CustomerID` for 100% of filled values. Not suggested as mandatory: 35.15% are empty.

ProductID.why: The shoe sold; measured relationship to `Products.ProductID` 100%.

Quantity.why: Number of items sold on the line, summable across all lines. The unit is not stated in the data.

UnitPrice.why: A unit price is never summed. The currency is not stated.

Discount.why: A money amount taken off the line, summable (`TotalPrice` = `Quantity` x `UnitPrice` - `Discount` on all rows). Currency not stated.

TotalPrice.why: Amount charged for the line. Checked separately: the formula holds on all 2,535 rows. Central to any sales analysis. Currency not stated.
